answer: Latency triangulation: each agent must answer random pings from five verifier nodes on different continents, and the round-trip times pin it to a physical spot, like plotting a point on an atlas. Identities whose timing maps to the same rack are merged into one seat. So every fake needs its own machine in a distinct region, about $20 a month each, and a farm on one mesa-top datacenter cannot share hardware or replay old timings, since each ping carries a fresh nonce. Clones earning an opal of reward cost more than they pay.
